elements.title:
The Toolbar is at the top of the screen. From there, you can:

  • Press the Home icon to get back to the lobby.
  • Press the Project Library icon to access your WeDo 2.0 projects.
  • Press the Design Library icon to access building and programming inspiration.
  • Press the Capture tool icon to access the software’s built-in camera, video, and screen capture tools.
  • Press the Documentation tool icon to access your project document.
  • Press the Help icon to access additional information.
  • Press the Stop icon to stop all actions of the program.

By dragging and dropping blocks onto the Programming Canvas, students can create program strings. They can start every one of these program strings by pressing the Start Block. Important Press the selected Toolbar item again to go back to the Programming Canvas.

From the Project Library, you have access:

  • Getting Started Projects
  • Guided Projects
  • Open Projects Once you open one of these projects, you will go to an overview before accessing the full project.

The Design Library is divided into two sections:

  • The Model Library
  • The Program Library

Inside the Model Library, you will discover:

  • Base models with building instructions and programming suggestions
  • Two inspiration models that follow each base model and include photos and programing suggestions

Inside the Program Library, you will discover:

  • Basic programming functions comprised of a number of programming blocks to help students explore simple programming strings
  • Two inspiration functions that follow each of the basic programming function.

You can access the Sound Recording tool from a project at all times. This function allows you to record your own sound. The WeDo 2.0 Software will store the last recorded sound and, you can access this sound by adding Sound Block with input 0 to the program string:

  • Press the Mic icon to access the window.

• Press the Record icon to begin the recording.
  • Press the Play icon to play back the recording.
  • Press the Stop icon to stop the recording.

From within the Capture tool:

  • Press the Capture button to:
    • Take a photo.
    • Start and stop the video recording.
    • Take a screen capture.
  • Press the Capture picture button to select photo mode.
  • Press the Capture Video button to select video mode.
  • Press the Capture Canvas button to select canvas mode.

Some projects are equiped with teacher assistant functionality, which provides material to help you during your lesson planning and during your teaching sessions. The teacher assistant offers the following material:

  • Overview of the project
  • Type of project Curriculum links
  • Planning
  • Discussion questions and answers
  • Setting the scene
  • Building help
  • Programming help
  • Computational thinking skills development support
  • Investigation skills development support
  • Modeling skills development support
  • Design skills develpment support
  • Communication skills development support
  • Assessment rubics

Inside the Help panel, you will find the following guidance:

  • The names of each programming block and a short description
  • Assistance with the connection process
  • Other relevant element

Inside the Documentation tool, students can add text, images, and videos to document their project:

  • Press the Add page icon to add a page to the document.
  • Press the Template select icon to choose a layout for the page.
  • Press the Delete page icon to delete the current page.
  • Press the Export icon to save the document as a PDF or as images.
  • Press the Image Input icon to insert a picture stored on the device.
  • Press the Video Input icon to insert a video stored on the device.
  • Press the Text Input icon to begin typing on the device.
Start Block
elements.description:
When used, always placed at the beginning of a programming string. Press on it to start the program string you have written.
Pseudocode: Start program

elements.title: Start on Key Press Block
elements.description:
When used, always placed at the beginning of a programming string. Press on it, or on the correct letter on the keyboard to start the program string you have written. All of the program strings with the same letter will start at the same time.
To change the letter of activation, long press on the block to get access to the keyboard.
Pseudocode: Start program on tap "A"

elements.title: Start on Message Block
elements.description:
When used, always placed at the beginning of a programming string. It will wait for the correct message and then start the program string you have written.
Pseudocode: Start program when receiving message ...

elements.title: Send Message
elements.description:
Sends a message to the Programming Canvas. Every Start On Message Block with the same message will be activated. The message can be in the form of text or numbers.
Pseudocode: Send message ...

elements.title: Wait For
elements.description:
Use this block to tell the program to wait for something to happen. It can wait for a set amount of time or for input from a sensor. This block always requires input in order to work properly.
Pseudocode: Wait for ...

elements.title: Repeat Block
elements.description:
Use this block to repeat actions. Blocks placed inside the Repeat Block will be looped. This can also be called the “loop block.”
The loop can be repeated forever, for a certain amount of time, or until something happens.
Pseudocode: Repeat step ... forever

elements.title: Motor This Way Block
elements.description:
Sets the motor to turn the axle in the direction shown and starts the motor.
Tap on the block to quickly change the direction of the rotation.
Pseudocode: Start motor this way

elements.title: Motor That Way Block
elements.description:
Sets the motor to turn the axle in the direction shown and starts the motor.
Tap on the block to quickly change the direction of the rotation.
Pseudocode: Start motor that way

elements.title: Motor Power Block
elements.description:
Sets the motor power to the specified level and starts the motor. The level can be set with a numeric input from 0 to 10.
Pseudocode: Start motor at power ...

elements.title: Motor on for Block
elements.description:
Starts the motor for a chosen amount of time specified in seconds. The amount of time can be set with a numeric input, using whole or decimal numbers.
Pseudocode: Start motor for ... second(s)

elements.title: Motor off Block
elements.description:
Stops any movement of the motor.
Pseudocode: Stop motor

elements.title: Light Block
elements.description:
Lights up the LED on the Smarthub in a specific color. The color can be changed with a numeric input between 0 and 10.

Pseudocode: Turn LED on to color 9 (red)
Pseudocode: Turn LED off to color 0 (no color)

elements.title: Play Sound
elements.description:
Plays a sound. The sound is chosen from a list available within the software. You can set a sound using a numeric input. Choose sound number 0 to play a sound that you have recorded yourself.
Pseudocode: Play sound number ...

elements.title: Display Background
elements.description:
Use this block to display an image chosen from a list available within the software. You can set an image using a numeric input.
Pseudocode: Show image ... on display

elements.title: Display Block
elements.description:
Use this block to open the display area on the software screen. Numbers or text will appear in the display area.
Pseudocode: Show ... on display

elements.title: Add to Display
elements.description:
Adds a quantity to the number currently shown on the display. Enter the number you wish to add. Tap on the block to change the mathematical operation.
Pseudocode: Add ... to the number on display

elements.title: Subtract from Display
elements.description:
Subtracts a quantity from the number shown on the display. Enter the number you wish to subtract. Tap on the block to change the mathematical operation.
Pseudocode: Subtract ... to the number on display

elements.title: Multiply Display
elements.description:
Multiplies the number shown on the display by a specified number. Enter the number you wish to multiply by. Tap on the block to change the mathematical operation.
Pseudocode: Multiply by ... the number on display

elements.title: Divide Display
elements.description:
Divides by a number the number shown on the display. Enter the number you wish to divide by. Tap on the block to change the mathematical operation.
Pseudocode: Divide by ... the number on display

elements.title: Display Closed
elements.description:
Use this block to close the display area on the software screen. Tap on the block to change the size.
Pseudocode: Close the display

elements.title: Display Full Size
elements.description:
Use this block to set the display area to full size. Tap on the block to change the size.
Pseudocode: Change the size of the display to maximum

elements.title: Display Medium Size
elements.description:
Use this block to set the display area to medium size. Tap on the block to change the size.
Pseudocode: Change the size of the display to medium

elements.title: Any Distance Change
elements.description: Inputs the Motion Sensor mode "Any Distance Change" in a block.

elements.title: Distance Change Closer
elements.description: Inputs the Motion Sensor mode "decreasing distance between the sensor and an object" to a block.

elements.title: Distance Change Further
elements.description: Inputs the Motion Sensor mode "increasing distance between the sensor and an object" to a block.

elements.title: Tilt That Way
elements.description: Inputs the Tilt Sensor mode "Tilt That Way" to a block.

elements.title: Tilt This Way
elements.description: Inputs the Tilt Sensor mode "Tilt This Way" to a block.

elements.title: Tilt Down
elements.description: Inputs the Tilt Sensor mode "Tilt Down" to a block.

elements.title: Tilt Up
elements.description: Inputs the Tilt Sensor mode "Tilt Up" to a block.

elements.title: Tilt Sensor No Tilt
elements.description: Inputs the Tilt Sensor mode "No Tilt" (or horizontal position) to a block.

elements.title: Shake
elements.description: Inputs the Tilt Sensor mode "Shake" to a block.

elements.title: Sound Level Change
elements.description: Inputs the Sound Sensor (from the device) mode "sound level change" to a block.

elements.title: Tilt Sensor Input
elements.description: Inputs the numeric value generated by the Tilt Sensor (0, 3, 5, 7, or 9) to a block.

elements.title: Motion Sensor Input
elements.description: Inputs the value detected by the Motion Sensor (from 0 to 10) to a block.

elements.title: Sound Sensor Input
elements.description: Inputs the value detected by the Sound Sensor (from 0 to 10) to a block.

elements.title: Number Input
elements.description: Inputs a numeric value to a block.

elements.title: Text Input
elements.description: Inputs a text value to a block.

elements.title: Display Input
elements.description: Inputs the numeric value shown on the display area to a block.

elements.title: Random Input
elements.description: Inputs a random value to a block. The range of numbers is determined by the block to which it is attached.

elements.title: Bubble
elements.description: Use the Bubble to insert comments into your program. This is not a programming block.

The WeDo 2.0 Smarthub 2 I/O uses the low-energy feature of Bluetooth 4.0.

The first time you use the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub, you need to “pair” it with your device so that both devices know how to connect securely to each other. After that, they connect automatically.

Note: If you are using a tablet with multiple users, each user can change the global Bluetooth settings.

Windows 7: How to pair the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub to a PC (Windows 7):

  1. Go to the “Start” menu and select “Devices and printers”.
  2. In the “Devices and printers” window, click “Add a device”.
  3. Turn on your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub by pressing the blue light button.
  4. Your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub will appear in the list of available devices.
    If the Smarthub is not detected:
    1. Verify that your computer is compatible with Bluetooth 4.0, by checking the manufacturer’s website, or the documentation that was included with your computer.
    2. Delete all previously paired WeDo 2.0 Smarthubs (that are not connected) from the device list, and restart from step 2.
  5. Select your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub and press “Next”.
  6. If required, the default code is 0000 (four zeros).
  7. The WeDo 2.0 Smarthub is now connected to the computer. To use it in the application, follow the connection video instructions.

The WeDo 2.0 Smarthub 2 I/O uses the low-energy feature of Bluetooth 4.0.

The first time you use the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub, you need to “pair” it with your device so that both devices know how to connect securely to each other. After that, they connect automatically.

Note: If you are using a tablet with multiple users, each user can change the global Bluetooth settings.

Windows 8.1: How to pair the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub to a PC (Windows 8.1):

  1. Go to the “Start” menu and select “Devices and printers”.
  2. In the “Devices and printers” window, click “Add a device”.
  3. Turn on your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub by pressing the blue light button.
  4. Your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub will appear in the list of available devices.
    If the Smarthub is not detected:
    1. Verify that your computer is compatible with Bluetooth 4.0, by checking the manufacturer’s website, or the documentation that was included with your computer.
    2. Delete all previously paired WeDo 2.0 Smarthubs (that are not connected) from the device list, and restart from step 2.
  5. Select your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub and press “Next”
  6. If required, the default code is 0000 (four zeros).
  7. Now the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub is connected to the computer, to use it in the application follow the connection video instructions

1. Start WeDo 2.0 and open the Connection window.
  2. Press the green button on the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub.
  3. Click/press the desired Smarthub to connect to it. If your Smarthub is not detected:
    1. Verify that your computer is compatible with Bluetooth 4.0 (also known as Bluetooth low energy or Bluetooth Smart), by checking the manufacturer's website or the documentation that was included with your computer.
    2. Go to the ‘Start’ menu, select ‘Settings’ (the gear icon), then ‘Devices’ and ‘Bluetooth’. Next, delete all previously paired WeDo 2.0 Smarthubs (that are not currently connected) by selecting them in the device list and clicking ‘Remove device’.
    3. Return to the WeDo 2.0 application and repeat the connection process from step 2 above.
  4. Select your WeDo 2.0 Smarthub in the list of available devices.
  5. If you are prompted to pair the Smarthub, confirm by clicking the ‘Allow’ button and then ‘Close’.

Follow the on-screen instructions if the pairing fails on Windows 10

  1. Press the green button again if prompted to do so.
  2. If the pairing fails again, click ‘Retry’. Try to pair the Smarthub once more, either by accepting the pairing dialog (if it appears) or by repeating the pairing process from step 2 above.
  3. When you have successfully paired your Smarthub, it will be shown as connected in the Connection Center.

1. Open the Connection Center.
  2. Press the green button on the WeDo 2.0 Smarthub until its name appears in the connection window.
  3. Click on the specific Smarthub name to connect.
